item.content:encoded:
To this day, this is still probably my favorite tale on the website. It’s so simply written and has such a unique structure. but still perfectly conveys the entire idea of the “greater good” that the Foundation is built on. This single short article defines the entire purpose of the Foundation in such a perfect, unique way.
No matter how many times I’ve read it, the last four lines never fail to give me chills.

To me, this singular article defines what the Foundation has to do in order to keep reality from falling apart. Sure, there are things done — tests performed — that are ethically ‘evil’, but that ‘evil’ is a necessity. Look at SCP-231. That is the greatest example of the Foundation doing something ‘evil’ to a single person in order to save the human race.

Think about it. If you had to choose between the life of a stranger and the lives of your loved ones, you'd sacrifice the stranger.

+1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm glad OnjEntertainment asked this question above me for one simple reason.

Ok
Well...

"There has to be a deeper meaning to this!"

Well, that just bloody says it all doesn't it. Because here's a secret…

There isn't

It attempts to reference a bunch of SCP's and be all arty and meaningful, but it feels like what would happen if you took a bunch of topics from this website's best works and walked past a poet, instead filtering them into a robot for it to just give out bland facts about a bunch of articles that like 90% of readers know about anyway. There are no points for discussion, no ambiguity, nothing interesting or mysterious or really even that much reflection on any points. And that is one of the greatest disappointments that I've ever seen. I thought I'd save this for a good day, you know, read the foundation's greatest tale! But was that what I got?

No. In fact, all of this is just a character listing off his events, I looked through and I think he only reacts about once in the whole thing. I get that the agents are meant to be cold, but shouldn't THAT be a point here, that behind the tough exterior, they're actually being torn apart on the inside by all that they see. I could take almost any good poem I'd say about 30% of people have never heard of like "Hummingbird" or "Science Fiction Cradlesong". You could keep discovering different messages through the intricately woven spiderwebs of hidden meaning that dwell within those poems, in this, here's the only mystery: "What are the SCP's are they referencing?"

A mystery that's solved in about 3 minutes at most. That's all, this story or diary or poem or whatever doesn't actually have any point to it. In fact, I've realised something now, the writer of the diary barely even reacts to a single one of these things, it's just them listing off a bunch of stuff that we all know already happens at the foundation.

And then we get to the fourth last line…

You want happy endings? Fuck you.

This is an attempt to emulate the entire foundation's deal: Oh yeah! We're all dark and we do subversions of expectations and no happy endings here, we're all super cool and edgy.

That is not what the foundation is. But that is the message this gives (bars). It tries to be all dark and cool and edgy and subvert our expectations, but it doesn't, again it's the most wooden line in the whole thing. This is a perfect representation of how absolutely wooden this entire thing feels and I would be lying if I said that I genuinely didn't cringe after my first read. The only thing that this gives a message of is that the factuality of this post parallels the factuality of the SCP articles on this site. BUT THAT'S WHAT MAKES IT A BAD TALE. I don't want to be mean here, but the writer of this should either get some actual inspiration and good topics that can be discussed and argued, or they should just stick to writing articles because honestly, they have the writing for that down, it just shouldn't be here as a meaningful writing piece, it feels like a report.


In short, I don't like this tale.
-1 as hard as possible.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Because lots of people have been asking which SCPs this story references, I'll try to list them to the best of my knowledge.

+ show block
– hide block

Yesterday,
I watched three men die because one man sneezed in a room full of blood and shit and light.
Today,
three more men go in, cheap mops and each other's lives in their hands.

SCP-173, obviously.

Yesterday,
I watched a man I admired gunned down for leaving a rose for a girl whose life was tattered by trauma she never deserved.
Today,
she doesn't remember, and three halls down I can hear her screaming.

SCP-231-7 is the girl, Decency is where the whole incident with the rose transpired.

Yesterday,
I watched a group of soldiers go down fighting against the corpses of comrades who'd died before them.
Today,
we test another sample, this time on children.

SCP-008.

Yesterday,
I watched five men and women gunned down in an abandoned factory no one cares about.
Today,
it happens again and again. Every eleven seconds. Forever.

SCP-176.

Yesterday,
I watched a man sit comfortably in a nice armchair, sipping scotch and laughing as he ordered a woman to simply stop breathing.
Today,
he gets the day off of work detail for good behavior.

SCP-209.

Yesterday,
I watched hundreds of men and women in orange jumpsuits herded like animals into empty rooms that filled with gas and fire.
Today,
hundreds more are told they have a chance for a lighter sentence, and a chance to serve their country.

D-Class end-of-the-month terminations.
The rest should be easy.
